title: Double, Double, Double: The 8s
goal: I can find any ×8 fact by doubling three times.

card.desc: Bailey learns that ×4 is double, double and ×8 is double, double, double (8 × 7: 14, 28, 56). Three quick doubles replace adding 8 over and over, which is where she loses track. New words: double, halve, quadruple, hoard, gargantuan, formidable, amplify.

win: Three doubles and done. You are a formidable fact finder!

slides.title: Double, Double, Double on Your Own
slides.text: In class you learned to double your way to the 4s and 8s. Now do it on your own. You will type most answers. Finish with Show What You Know.

slides.title: Count the doubles
slides.text: Read this once. Then you are ready.

visual.text:
✌️ ×2: double once. 2 × 9 → 18
✌️✌️ ×4: double twice. 4 × 9 → 18 → 36
✌️✌️✌️ ×8: double three times. 8 × 9 → 18 → 36 → 72
➕ Big doubles: tens, then ones. 36 + 36 → 60 + 12 = 72

slides.tip: Doubling means add the number to itself. 14 doubled is 14 + 14, not 14 + 7.

slides.title: Your 7 words
slides.text: Flip each card one more time. Next you will type these words from memory.

words.meaning: to make something two times as big; to multiply by 2
to cut something into two equal parts; to divide by 2
to make something four times as big
a large pile of things someone has saved and hidden
words.example: The dragon slept on a hoard of gold coins.
A gargantuan sea dragon rose out of the waves.

words.meaning: so strong or powerful that people are afraid of it or respect it
words.example: The Viking chief was a formidable warrior.

words.meaning: to make something bigger, louder, or stronger
words.example: Hiccup cupped his hands to amplify his voice.

slides.title: Type the word
slides.text: Type the word that fits. Spell it carefully.

items.q: Which word means to make something four times as big?
items.why: Quadruple means four times as big. It is double, then double again.
items.no: Think of a quad bike: four wheels.

items.q: Which word means to make something bigger, louder, or stronger?
items.why: To amplify is to make bigger, louder, or stronger.
items.no: Look back at the word cards. It starts with a.

items.q: Fishlegs kept a secret ____ of honey cakes under his bed.
items.why: A hoard is a big pile of things someone has saved and hidden.
items.no: Which word means a pile of saved, hidden things?

items.q: Halve 30 and you get 15. ____ 15 and you get 30 again.
items.why: To double is to make two times as big: 15 + 15 = 30. Double undoes halve.
items.no: Which word is the opposite of halve?

slides.title: Finish the chain
slides.text: Type the missing number.

slides.title: How many doubles?
slides.text: Tap a fact. Then tap the box for how many times you double the other number. Turn it around if you need to.

items.hint: The 4 tells you how many doubles. How many doubles make ×4?
Turn it around to 8 × 9. How many doubles make ×8?
The 2 tells you how many doubles. ×2 is double one time.
Turn it around to 4 × 3. How many doubles make ×4?
The 8 tells you how many doubles. How many doubles make ×8?
Turn it around to 2 × 5. ×2 is double one time.

slides.done: ×2 = one double. ×4 = two doubles. ×8 = three doubles.

slides.title: Teach someone at home
slides.text: Find someone at home. Teach them for two minutes.
prompts: Show them how to find 8 × 9 with three doubles. Count the doubles on your fingers.
Show them how to double 36 with tens and ones.
Tell them about something gargantuan or formidable in your book.
starters: Double the tens: … Double the ones: …
In my book, … is formidable because …

slides.title: Doubling on Berk
slides.text: Find the equal groups. Then double.

items.q: 8 dragons each breathe 7 fireballs. How many fireballs in all?
items.no: 8 equal groups of 7. Double 7 three times.

items.q: Hiccup has 4 baskets with 8 eggs in each. 5 eggs crack. How many eggs are not cracked?
items.no: First find all the eggs (4 × 8). Then take away 5.

items.q: A rowboat is 9 feet long. A gargantuan sea dragon is 8 times as long. Which chain finds its length?
items.why: 8 times as long is 8 × 9. Three doubles of 9: 18, 36, 72 feet.
no: "Times as long" means multiply, not add.
That adds 9 each time. Double 18 means 18 + 18.
That is 4 × 8 = 32. Double the 9 three times.

sets.q: Which chain shows 4 × 8?
no: 16 + 8 = 24 adds an 8. Doubling 16 is 16 + 16.
That is three doubles. ×4 is only two.
That adds 4 each time. ×4 means double the 8 twice.

sets.q: A gargantuan sea dragon rose from the waves. Which word means almost the same as gargantuan?
sets.why: Gargantuan means giant-sized, so enormous is closest.
no: Gargantuan is about size, not mood.
Gargantuan is about size, not age.
Gargantuan is about size, not sound.

sets.q: Each Viking shield has 4 iron studs. Hiccup polishes 9 shields. How many studs does he polish?
sets.no: 9 shields with 4 studs each. ×4 is double, double.

sets.q: What is 8 × 3?
no: 11 is 8 + 3. Multiply.
21 is 7 × 3. One more 3.

sets.q: Which word means so strong or powerful that people fear or respect it?
sets.why: Formidable: so powerful that people fear or respect it.

sets.no: 8 times what is 48? Try doubling a number three times.

sets.q: Bailey knows 8 × 9 = 72. She halves 72. Which fact does she get?
sets.why: Half of 8 groups is 4 groups. 4 × 9 = 36, and 36 is half of 72.
no: Half of 72 is 36, not 32.
Halving makes it smaller, not bigger.
64 is not half of 72.

sets.q: The tribe has 8 longships with 9 Vikings on each. Then 6 Vikings stay home sick. How many Vikings sail?
sets.no: First find all the Vikings (8 × 9). Then take away 6.

sets.q: Which chain shows 4 × 7?
no: 14 + 7 = 21 adds a 7. Doubling 14 is 14 + 14.
That is three doubles, which is ×8.
That adds 4 each time. Double the 7 twice.

sets.q: The dragon slept on its hoard. What is a hoard?
choices: a big pile of saved, hidden treasure
sets.why: A hoard is a large pile of things someone has saved and hidden.
no: A hoard is a pile of saved things, not a bed.
A hoard is a pile, not a sound.
A hoard is a pile of saved things, not a mountain.

sets.q: The Berk blacksmith makes 4 swords a day for 7 days. How many swords does he make?
sets.no: 7 days with 4 swords each. ×4 is double, double.

sets.q: What is 8 × 4?
no: 12 is 8 + 4. Multiply.

sets.q: Which word means huge; far bigger than usual?
sets.why: Gargantuan means huge, far bigger than usual.

sets.q: Bailey knows 8 × 4 = 32. She halves the 8 to get 4 × 4. What is 4 × 4?
no: 64 is double 32. Halving makes it smaller.
8 is 2 × 4. 4 × 4 is two doubles: 8, 16.

sets.q: Stoick has 8 crates with 7 apples in each crate. The dragons eat 9 apples. How many apples are left?
sets.no: First find all the apples (8 × 7). Then take away 9.
Turn it around to 8 × 9. Double 9 three times.

sets.q: Which chain shows 8 × 5?
no: That adds 5 each time. Double means add the number to itself.
That is only two doubles, which is ×4.
That is 8 × 8. Double the 5, not the 8.

sets.no: Turn it around to 8 × 6. Double 6 three times.

sets.q: Hiccup cupped his hands to amplify his voice. What happened to his voice?
sets.why: To amplify is to make bigger, louder, or stronger.
no: Amplify makes something bigger or louder, not quieter.
Amplify is about bigger or louder, not higher.
A louder voice is the opposite of a secret.

sets.q: Fishlegs reads 4 pages each night for 8 nights. How many pages does he read?
sets.no: 8 nights with 4 pages each. Double 8 twice.

sets.q: What is 4 × 6?
no: 18 is 3 × 6. Double, double.
12 is only one double.

sets.q: Which word means to cut into two equal parts?
sets.why: To halve is to cut into two equal parts, or divide by 2.
sets.no: It starts with h. It is the opposite of double.

sets.q: Toothless had 3 fish. Hiccup quadrupled them. How many fish does Toothless have now?
no: Quadruple does not mean add 4.
6 is only doubled once.
9 is 3 times as many. Quadruple is 4 times.

sets.q: The Berk blacksmith makes 8 shields with 9 studs on each. 10 studs fall off. How many studs are still on?
sets.no: First find all the studs (8 × 9). Then take away 10.

practice.intro: Three tries on each one. Only your first try counts. Type most answers. Count your doubles on your fingers.

no: That chain adds 3 each time. 12 is only 4 × 3.
Two doubles make ×4, so 12 is 4 × 3. Double one more time.

questions.q: Hiccup starts with 7 and doubles three times. Which fact did he find?
no: Three doubles is not ×3. Each double is ×2, and 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.
Doubling three times multiplies by 8, not 6.

choices: Hiccup hoarded across the beach to catch the boat.
The dragon guarded its hoard of gold deep in the cave.
The hoard of the song was too loud.
questions.why: A hoard is a big pile of saved, hidden things, like a dragon's gold.
no: Hoard is not a way of moving. A hoard is a pile of saved things.
A song does not have a hoard. A hoard is a hidden pile of treasure or supplies.

questions.q: The Berk forge has 8 shelves. Each shelf holds 6 helmets. How many helmets?
questions.no: 8 equal groups of 6. Double 6 three times.

questions.q: A Viking had 5 coins. Then he quadrupled them. How many coins does he have now?
questions.no: Quadruple means four times as many. Double, then double again.

questions.q: Bailey knows 8 × 7 = 56. She halves 56. Which fact does she get?
questions.why: Half of 56 is 28. Half of 8 groups is 4 groups, so 4 × 7 = 28.
no: Half of 8 is 4, so the 8 becomes 4 and the 7 stays.
Halving 56 gives 28, not 49.

questions.q: Fishlegs says, "8 × 6 is 6, 12, 18. So 8 × 6 = 18." What should he have done?
no: Four doubles is ×16. Three doubles is ×8.
Starting with 6 is fine. The mistake is adding 6 instead of doubling.

questions.q: The horn will ____ the chief's call so the whole island hears it.
questions.why: Amplify means make bigger, louder, or stronger.
questions.no: Which word means make louder? It starts with a.

pages.title: Part 1: Doubling chains
pages.directions: Fill in each chain. Two doubles make ×4. Three doubles make ×8. Then write the fact.

pages.title: Part 2: Draw it
pages.directions: Draw an array of dots. Then answer.

items.text: 5. Draw 4 rows of 7 dots. Circle the top 2 rows.
6. The top 2 rows show 2 × 7 = ____. Double it: 4 × 7 = ____
7. Explain to a friend why doubling three times is the same as ×8.

pages.title: Part 3: Word power
pages.directions: Draw a line from each word to its meaning.

right: to make bigger, louder, or stronger
so powerful that people fear or respect it
to make four times as big
to cut into two equal parts

items.text: 14. Use the word hoard in a sentence about a dragon.

pages.title: Part 4: Word problems
pages.directions: Write the fact. Show your doubling chain. Write the answer with a label.

items.text: 15. Stoick has 8 barrels. Each barrel holds 6 fish. How many fish?
16. Hiccup feeds Toothless 4 crabs a day for 9 days. How many crabs?
17. A Viking trader has 8 racks with 7 axes on each rack. He sells 6 axes. How many axes are left?

teacher.objective: Bailey finds ×4 facts by doubling twice and ×8 facts by doubling three times (8 × 7: 14, 28, 56), so she stops adding 8 over and over and losing count. She also learns seven new words (double, halve, quadruple, hoard, gargantuan, formidable, amplify).
materials: Zoom with screen share: you share this class lesson; she answers out loud and you tap or type her answer (or give her remote control)
At home: about 60 dried beans (or cereal pieces), a sheet of paper, a pencil, and paper or a small whiteboard to hold up
Her book, How to Train Your Dragon
Your own whiteboard on camera to model doubling chains

plan.do: Class slide 1. Share your screen. Check she has beans, paper and pencil. Quick warm-up: 7 + 7 and 14 + 14.
Class slide 2. She retells in order and names Hiccup's biggest problem and the type of conflict.
Class slide 3. She says the shortcut out loud before each answer.
Class slides 4–5. Teach the 7 words one at a time; she writes each on paper and makes a book sentence. Slide 5: she says why the wrong choices are wrong.
Class slides 6–7. At home she builds 1 row of 6 beans, doubles it, doubles again, and holds it up. She says each double out loud.
Class slides 8–9. She says each double before you reveal it. Practice big doubles (24 + 24, 32 + 32) by tens and ones on paper.
Class slides 10–11. 8 piles of 6 beans at home; top half is 4 × 6, so double 24. Then she orders the 8 × 9 chain aloud.
Class slides 12–13. Fingers up for the number of doubles before typing. She writes each chain on paper before tapping.
Class slide 14. She explains why three doubles is ×8, makes up an 8 × 4 dragon problem, and halves 8 × 7.
Class slide 15. Show the task list: tonight is only the After-Class Lesson (with Show What You Know) and 10 minutes of reading.

watch: Adding the start number instead of doubling (7, 14, 21, 28). Say: "Double means add the number to itself. What is 14 + 14?"
Losing count of the doubles. Have her hold up one finger per double and stop at three.
Doubling a 2-digit number (28 + 28) slowly. Break it: 20 + 20 = 40, 8 + 8 = 16, 40 + 16 = 56.
"I can't do it." Point back to the chain: "You only need three steps. Do the first one."
Mixing up quadruple (×4) and the ×8 fact. Ask: how many doubles is quadruple?

packet_key.answer: 4 rows of 7 dots, top 2 rows circled
Each double is ×2, and 2 × 2 × 2 = 8. (Or: 2 groups, then 4 groups, then 8 groups.)
halve: to cut into two equal parts
quadruple: to make four times as big
formidable: so powerful that people fear or respect it
amplify: to make bigger, louder, or stronger
Any sentence that uses hoard as a pile of saved things, e.g. "The dragon hid its hoard of gold in a cave."

teacher.notes: Show What You Know is at the end of the After-Class Lesson, done at home tonight; a retake gives a brand-new set of 10. Tomorrow (Lesson 4) is in person: check the course page for her score first. If she is under 90, start Lesson 4 by rebuilding 8 rows of 7 with counters, splitting it into halves and quarters to show each double, then have her retake the check. This lesson's Practice and Packet are assigned on Lesson 4's task list, so check the packet on Thursday.

tasks: Monday night: do the After-Class Lesson. Get 90 or more on Show What You Know.
Monday night: read How to Train Your Dragon for 10 minutes. Find one thing that is gargantuan or formidable.

slides.title: Double, Double, Double: The 8s
slides.text: Last week you tamed the 9s and the 6s. Today you get a new tool: doubling. With three quick doubles you can find every ×8 fact without adding 8 over and over.

visual.sub: Three doubles will get you there.

notes.do: Zoom: share your screen with this class lesson. Before you start, check that she has at home: about 60 dried beans (or cereal pieces), a sheet of paper, a pencil, and paper or a small whiteboard to hold up to the camera.
notes.say: "Last week you tamed the 9s and the 6s. This week we take on the 8s. Today's tool is doubling, and you already know how to double."
notes.listen: 14 and 28 quickly. If 14 + 14 is slow, plan extra time on class slide 9 (doubling bigger numbers).

slides.title: How does Hiccup solve problems?
slides.text: Think about the part of How to Train Your Dragon you read since our last lesson.
prompts: Tell me what happened, in order: beginning, middle, end.
What is the biggest problem Hiccup faces right now? Is it with another character, with himself, or with nature?
Hiccup is not the biggest or strongest Viking. What does he use instead of muscles?

notes.do: 5–7 minutes. She holds the book up to the camera and finds the page where she stopped.
notes.say: "Hiccup is not the biggest Viking. Today we are going to be like Hiccup: use a smart tool instead of muscles."
notes.ask: "What is Hiccup's biggest problem right now? Is it with another character, with himself, or with nature?"
notes.listen: Retelling with order words (first, then, at the end) and a named conflict type with a reason. If she says only "a dragon," ask "What makes it hard for HIM?"

slides.title: Last week's shortcuts
slides.text: Use your ×9 and ×6 tools. No adding over and over!

items.q: What is 9 × 7? Use ×10 minus one group.
no: 72 is 9 × 8. Start from 70 and take away one 7.
You took away 9. Take away one group of 7: 70 − 7.
You took away two 7s. Nine groups is only one group less than ten.

items.q: 6 × ? = 48. Use ×5 plus one group to test each choice.
Bailey says 9 × 6 = 54. Which is a way to verify it?
items.why: To verify is to check that it is true. The digits of a 9s fact add to 9, and the ×10 shortcut gives 54 too.
no: Looking right is a guess, not a check.
9 + 6 = 15 adds the factors. It does not check 54 at all.

notes.do: She says the tool out loud before she taps ("70 take away 7").
notes.ask: "What does verify mean? How did you verify 9 × 6 = 54?"
notes.listen: "Check that it's true." Two checks: digits add to 9, and 60 − 6. If she starts adding 9s, stop her: "What is 10 groups?"

slides.title: Seven words for today
slides.text: Jonathan flips each card. Read the meaning out loud. Then make your own sentence.

words.meaning: to make something two times as big; to multiply by 2
to cut something into two equal parts; to divide by 2
to make something four times as big
a large pile of things someone has saved and hidden
words.example: The dragon slept on a hoard of gold coins.
A gargantuan sea dragon rose out of the waves.

words.meaning: so strong or powerful that people are afraid of it or respect it
words.example: The Viking chief was a formidable warrior.

words.meaning: to make something bigger, louder, or stronger
words.example: Hiccup cupped his hands to amplify his voice.

notes.do: Teach one word at a time (about 1 minute each). She writes each word on paper at home to start a new word list for this week.
notes.say: "Double means two times as many. Halve is the opposite: cut into two equal parts. Quadruple has quad in it, like a quad bike with four wheels: four times as big. A hoard is a hidden pile, like a dragon's gold. Gargantuan means giant-sized. Formidable means so powerful people respect or fear it. Amplify means make bigger or louder, like a speaker."
notes.ask: "How are double and quadruple related?" "Who in the book is formidable?" "What would a dragon keep in its hoard?"
notes.listen: "Quadruple is double, then double again." Book sentences like "Stoick is formidable."

items.q: Which sentence uses formidable correctly?
choices: The tiny kitten was formidable, so nobody noticed it.
Fishlegs ate a formidable breakfast of toast.
The Vikings stepped back from the formidable dragon.
items.why: Formidable means powerful enough to make people afraid or respectful. Stepping back shows that.
no: Something formidable gets noticed and makes people careful. A tiny kitten nobody noticed is the opposite.
Toast cannot make anyone afraid or respectful. Formidable is about power.

items.q: Hiccup had 7 fish. Then he quadrupled them. Which shows the new number?
items.why: Quadruple means four times as many: 7 × 4 = 28. That is double (14), then double again (28).
no: Quadruple does not mean add 4. It means four times as many.
14 is only doubled once. Quadruple is double, then double again.
56 is three doubles. Quadruple is only two doubles.

items.q: Halve is the opposite of which word? Type it.
items.why: To double is to make two times as big. To halve is to cut in two. They undo each other.
items.no: Halve means cut into two equal parts. What is its opposite?

notes.do: She reads each sentence out loud first and tells you why the wrong choices are wrong. You tap or type the answer she says.
notes.ask: "Why can't toast be formidable?" "If I quadruple 7 and you double 7, who has more? How many more?"
notes.listen: "Toast isn't powerful." "You have 28 and I have 14, so 14 more."

slides.title: Stepping stone: ×4 is double, double
slides.text: Doubling means ×2. If you double, and then double again, you have multiplied by 4, because 2 × 2 = 4.
slides.tip: Two doubles = ×4. Say it while you count on two fingers: "double, double."

notes.do: Hands-on at home: she puts 1 row of 6 beans on her paper. "Double it": she makes a second row (12). "Double again": she copies both rows (24 in 4 rows).
notes.say: "Each double is ×2. Two doubles is ×2 ×2, and that is ×4."
notes.ask: "How many rows do you have now? How many beans? So what is 4 × 6?"
notes.listen: "4 rows, 24 beans, 4 × 6 = 24." Have her hold the paper up to the camera.

items.q: What is 4 × 7? Double, then double again.
no: 21 is 7 + 7 + 7. That is only 3 groups.
Double 14 means 14 + 14. Try that again.
14 is only one double (2 × 7). Double once more.

items.q: Which chain shows 4 × 9?
no: 18 + 9 = 27 adds a 9. Doubling 18 means 18 + 18.
That chain doubles three times. That is ×8, not ×4.

notes.do: She says each double out loud while holding up a finger for each one.

slides.title: The big one: ×8 is double, double, double
slides.text: Double three times and you have multiplied by 8, because 2 × 2 × 2 = 8. Watch 8 × 7.
slides.tip: Count the doubles on three fingers. Three doubles is only three steps. Adding up eight 7s takes seven steps, with seven chances to lose your place.

notes.do: Reveal one step at a time. She says each double BEFORE you click to show it. Three fingers up by the end.
notes.say: "Three doubles is ×8, because 2 × 2 × 2 = 8. Three steps instead of adding up eight 7s."
notes.ask: "How many steps does it take to add up eight 7s? How many steps is doubling?"
notes.listen: "Seven adds" versus "three doubles." Point out: fewer steps means fewer places to lose count.

slides.title: Doubling bigger numbers
slides.text: The third double is often a 2-digit number, like 28 + 28. Double the tens, double the ones, then put them together.
slides.tip: Tens first, then ones. It is the same trick every time.

notes.do: Write 28 + 28 on your whiteboard and split it into tens and ones. Then say 24 + 24 and 32 + 32 and she does them on her paper and holds them up.
notes.listen: 48 and 64, with "40 and 8" or "60 and 4" said out loud. These are the third doubles for 8 × 6 and 8 × 8.

slides.title: Eight nests on the cliff
slides.text: On a cliff near Berk there are 8 dragon nests. Each nest holds 6 eggs. Build the nests.
slides.why: 8 groups of 6. Any 4 nests make 4 × 6 = 24. The other 4 nests make another 24, so double 24: 8 × 6 = 48.
slides.hint: The nests are the groups. The eggs in one nest go in each group. How many nests? How many eggs in each nest?

notes.do: On the shared screen you build the 8 nests as she tells you what to do. At home she makes 8 small piles of 6 beans at the same time, then pushes them into two rows of 4 piles.
notes.say: "Point to 4 of the nests. That is 4 × 6. The other 4 nests are the same."
notes.ask: "What is 4 × 6? Why can we just double 24?"
notes.listen: "24, and the other 4 nests are another 24, so 48."

slides.title: Find 8 × 9 by doubling
slides.text: Tap the steps in the right order.
slides.hint: Start with the number you double. After that, each double uses the number you just made.

notes.do: She tells you which step comes next and you tap it on the shared screen. She reads each step out loud.
notes.ask: "Which step is the hardest? How do you double 36?"

slides.title: Count the doubles
slides.text: Find the 2, 4 or 8. Turn the fact around if you need to.

items.q: 8 × 3: how many times do you double? Type a number.
items.no: Which number is 8? ×8 is three doubles.

items.q: 7 × 4: how many times do you double? Type a number.
items.no: Turn it around. ×4 is two doubles.

items.q: 2 × 9: how many times do you double? Type a number.
items.no: ×4 takes two doubles. How many does ×2 take?

items.q: 5 × 8: how many times do you double? Type a number.
items.no: Turn it around. Which number is 8?

notes.do: She holds up one finger per double, says the number, and then says the whole chain. You type her number.
notes.ask: "For 5 × 8, which number do you double? Why not double the 8?"
notes.listen: "Double the 5 three times, because the 8 tells me how many doubles."

items.q: Fishlegs tries 8 × 7. He writes: 7, 14, 21, 28. He says 8 × 7 = 28. What went wrong?
choices: He started with the wrong number.
He added 7 each time instead of doubling.
items.why: 14 + 7 = 21 adds one more 7. Doubling 14 is 14 + 14 = 28, then 28 + 28 = 56.
no: Starting with 7 is right. Look at the step from 14 to 21.
He only made three jumps. The problem is how he jumped: adding 7, not doubling.

items.q: The Hooligan tribe has 8 longships. Each longship carries 8 Vikings. How many Vikings sail?
no: 16 is 8 + 8. That counts only two ships.
72 is 8 × 9. There are 8 Vikings on each ship.

items.q: Each dragon in the pen has 4 legs. Hiccup counts the legs on 8 dragons. How many legs?
no: 12 is 8 + 4. Each dragon has 4 legs, so these are equal groups. Multiply.
16 is only two doubles. ×8 needs three.
36 is 9 × 4. There are 8 dragons.

notes.do: She reads each problem aloud, names the equal groups, and writes the chain on her paper before she taps.
notes.ask: For Fishlegs: "Where did he go wrong? Fix it out loud."
notes.listen: "14 + 7 adds a 7. He should do 14 + 14 = 28, then 56."

slides.title: Teach it back
slides.text: Now you are the teacher. Explain it to Jonathan.
prompts: Why is doubling three times the same as ×8?
Make up a dragon problem for 8 × 4. Use the word gargantuan or formidable.
8 × 7 = 56. If you halve the 8, what fact do you get?

notes.do: She holds up her paper with her dragon problem and the doubling chain.
notes.say: "If you can teach it, you own it."
notes.listen: "2 × 2 × 2 = 8." A problem with 8 equal groups of 4 (or 4 groups of 8) and the answer 32. "4 × 7 = 28, half of 56."

slides.title: Three doubles and done
slides.text: Today you learned that ×4 is double, double and ×8 is double, double, double.
